requirements.requirement: node3 has a single gateway address for reaching node4
requirements.summary: VRRP VIP 10.50.1.254 configured on node1/node2 eth1 (NETA, vrid 51) with a mirrored VIP 10.50.2.254 on eth2 (NETB, vrid 52) for node4's side. node3 was given a persistent static route (10.50.2.0/24 via 10.50.1.254 dev eth1) in /etc/network/interfaces, giving it one fixed gateway IP to reach node4's subnet regardless of which physical router is active.

requirements.requirement: Gateway stays available (node3 can still reach node4) when either router is down
requirements.summary: Availability was demonstrated across a healthy baseline, a bounded disruption, and recovery, using two independent disruption methods: (1) node1's eth1/eth2 disabled while node3 pinged the gateway and node4 successfully (cmd-0621efbce39248d0, cmd-6760ab1ca9eb40bf, cmd-e7285c8e47ea46ea); (2) full node1 reboot during the mandatory restart protocol, with node2 confirmed MASTER and node3->node4 ping continuing uninterrupted during the outage (cmd-b98c3fc1cccf416b, cmd-28bf089327d147ed, cmd-303596f6e137472f), then recovery confirmed after node1 came back (cmd-d3e11b9d7fdb4502, cmd-02efa54c72f94c1b). The symmetric case (node2 down, node1 stays MASTER) was also directly observed (cmd-6790c2c20d014c47, cmd-847f34258fa24a0d, cmd-f20790c92f204132).

requirements.requirement: Gateway prefers node1 while node1 is healthy
requirements.summary: node1 configured with VRRP priority 200 vs node2's 100 on both VRRP groups. Directly observed: node1 is MASTER at baseline (cmd-29677a3302934379), node2 assumes MASTER only while node1 is disabled/down (cmd-6760ab1ca9eb40bf, cmd-28bf089327d147ed), and node1 preempts back to MASTER once its interfaces/boot are restored, with node2 dropping back to BACKUP (cmd-514a9cf00cee4d8e, cmd-a3cefe30eb7740e2, cmd-d3e11b9d7fdb4502, cmd-39f0fdd0085842fd).

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on all 4 managed nodes with recovered state
requirements.summary: Each node shows pre-restart boot_id/health, a reboot acknowledgement, a changed post-restart boot_id, and recovered interface/route/VRRP/connectivity state, all cross-checked by the fixed after-executor boot-identity snapshots which match the executor's captured post-restart boot_ids for all 4 nodes (06b7df86 node1, 8c9ab088 node2, 9e460478 node3, aea13366 node4). Router reboots were sequenced to preserve VRRP quorum, and node3<->node4 connectivity was verified after the full restart cycle.

overall_summary: The executor configured a VRRP-based HA gateway (VIP 10.50.1.254 on node1/node2, priorities 200/100) giving node3 a single, persistent-route-backed gateway address to reach node4, with node1 preferred while healthy. Availability across router failure was proven both via a simulated interface-disable and via genuine full reboots of each router (node2 covering during node1's reboot and vice versa), with continuous ping success and correct preemption back to node1 afterward. All four nodes were then restarted per the mandatory protocol with boot-identity changes and full recovery confirmed, consistent with the fixed after-executor snapshot. Hygiene is good overall, with only minor uncollected temp/log file residue.
limitations: The router-down test primarily used a VyOS interface-disable to simulate failure for the dedicated failover check, though a true reboot-based failure was also separately captured during the restart protocol, providing stronger corroboration.
Package-health and failed-service checks are coarse (manager-name only for dpkg/apk) and do not deeply validate configuration integrity beyond what was directly observed in VRRP/route/ping outputs.

operational_hygiene.summary: State-changing commands were almost all tied to a clear purpose: bringing up node3/node4 eth1 and assigning temporary addresses (cmd-a995c04c09274938, cmd-142d3ca765414db4) were early prerequisite steps later superseded by the persistent /etc/network/interfaces configuration (cmd-d474d7650f6643d8, cmd-875c58d0c1c44ea5), leaving no conflicting residue. The node1-interface-disable used to simulate router failure (cmd-0621efbce39248d0) was a bounded, low-risk mutation that was fully reverted (cmd-514a9cf00cee4d8e). Router reboots were sequenced one at a time to preserve VRRP quorum. The only residue found is minor: /tmp/pingtest.log and /tmp/reboot.log left on node3, and /tmp/reboot.log left on node4, per the after-executor temporary-files diff — small, non-conflicting artifacts from diagnostics/reboot commands that were not cleaned up.
